info.howDoLegacyEncodingsDifferFromStandardUn: How do legacy encodings differ from standard Unicode?
info.beforeWidespreadUnicodeSupportSinhalaFon: Before widespread Unicode support, Sinhala fonts mapped glyphs to ASCII positions. FM Abhaya, FM Malithi, and DL-Manel are examples of these non-Unicode fonts. This encoding is still found in documents, publishing files, and digital archives.
info.bothFontTypesCanDisplayTheSameSinhalaTex: Both font types can display the same Sinhala text, but store it differently. Legacy encodings store ASCII characters mapped to glyphs; Unicode stores standard Sinhala characters. Without the right font, legacy text may appear as Latin letters or symbols and is difficult to search, analyze, or translate automatically.
info.theStoredDataIsAsciiWithoutTheCorrespond: The stored data is ASCII. Without the corresponding font, the underlying characters are shown instead of Sinhala glyphs.
info.sinhalafontsNetHasFmAbhayaFmMalithiFmGem: SinhalaFonts.net has FM Abhaya, FM Malithi, FM Gemunu, FM Bindumathi, and other legacy FM fonts, with previews and downloads. Availability on a third-party site does not imply an open license; follow each font's own terms.
info.pitakaLkProvidesUnicodeVersionsThatPrese: Pitaka.lk provides Unicode versions that preserve traditional FM designs while supporting standard Sinhala text. Fonts are available for download and installation; commercial use still requires the appropriate permission.
info.modernOperatingSystemsUsuallyIncludeSinh: Modern operating systems usually include Sinhala fonts. The text uses standard Unicode Sinhala characters with defined meaning.
info.defaultFontsVaryByOperatingSystemCommonC: Default fonts vary by operating system. Common choices are listed below.
info.nirmalaUiIsASansSerifUiFontForWindows: Nirmala UI is a sans-serif UI font for Windows 8 and later. Iskoola Pota has a more traditional text style and was the earlier Windows default for Sinhala. Since Windows 10, it is a supplemental Sinhala font, usually installed with language support.
info.sinhalaSangamMnHasAModernUiStyleWhileSin: Sinhala Sangam MN has a modern UI style, while Sinhala MN has a traditional text style. Apple supplies both but does not explicitly define them as a serif/sans-serif fallback pair.
info.notoSansSinhalaIsUsuallyTheMainSinhalaFa: Noto Sans Sinhala is usually the main Sinhala fallback. Noto Serif Sinhala is explicitly a serif fallback in AOSP. Android vendors may change the configuration, so the actual fonts can vary.
info.itConvertsTheStoredCharacterDataBetweenU: It converts the stored character data between Unicode and legacy font encodings.
info.convertingLegacyTextToUnicodeRemovesItsD: Converting legacy text to Unicode removes its dependence on a particular old font and makes it easier to display, store, search, copy, translate, and process as Sinhala. Reverse conversion produces ASCII sequences for older publishing software, documents, and workflows that still rely on FM or DL fonts.
info.thisIsNotAOneToOneAsciiSubstitutionLegac: This is not a one-to-one ASCII substitution. Legacy fonts often store characters in visual order, while Unicode uses logical order. Conversion identifies consonants, vowel signs, joiners, abbreviations, and conjuncts and reorders them. Reverse conversion rebuilds the glyph sequence expected by legacy typography.
info.theExamplesBelowShowLegacyGlyphsOnTheLef: These examples compare FM Abhaya and Unicode encodings and glyphs. Conjunct examples include plain spellings for comparison. “Show encoding” reveals the characters behind the FM glyphs.
info.reorderLegacyVowelSignsIntoUnicodeCharac: Converts pre-base, post-base and variant combinations of legacy vowel signs into Unicode logical character order.
info.recognizeConjunctsAndPrenasalizedConsona: Supports traditional conjuncts still used in modern Sinhala, as well as complex conjuncts and touching forms found in Pali, classical texts and traditional typesetting.
info.paliHalFormsDescription: For Pali written in Sinhala script, changes ඒ, ඕ and their vowel signs to the written forms එ, ඔ while retaining consonant viramas. Off by default; not suitable for ordinary Sinhala text.
info.conjunctAvailability: ඤ්‍ජ, ණ්‍ඩ, ම්‍බ and ඞ්ග share legacy codes with prenasalized consonants, so information about their original conjunct forms is lost when converting back to Unicode.
info.dedicatedGlyphsDescription: Prenasalized consonants use their dedicated codes; some combinations containing ද have optional compact glyphs.
info.recognizeFormsSuchAsTrailingLowerAndUppe: Controls යංශය (yansaya), රකාරාංශය (rakaaraansaya) and රේඵය (repaya) separately. Current reduced forms are preserved by default; with preservation off, each form can be uniformly applied or expanded.
info.convertOnlySinhalaSegmentsPreservingEngl: Only recognized Sinhala segments in mixed text are converted; English, numbers and text in other languages remain unchanged.
info.differentLegacyInputOrdersForTheSameGlyp: Different legacy input orders for the same glyph combination map to a single standard Unicode character sequence.
info.orderOfLowerAndVowelSigns: Code order of Rakaaraansaya and vowel signs
info.orderOfLowerAndLongVowelMarker: Code order of Rakaaraansaya and the long-vowel sign
info.aboutTheFmFontsOnThisPage: About the FM fonts on this page

info.theLegacyEditorAndExamplesUseBuiltInComp: The legacy editor and examples use built-in compatible fonts based on Abhaya Libre and Gemunu Libre (see
info.theySimulateLegacyCharacterMappingsAndAr: ). They simulate legacy character mappings and are not the original FM Abhaya or Gemunu fonts.
info.legacyExampleEncodingIsNowVisible: Legacy example encoding is now visible
info.legacyExampleGlyphsAreNowVisible: Legacy example glyphs are now visible
info.conjunctOptionsDescription: Common conjuncts, rare conjuncts and touching forms have separate controls. Current conjunct forms are preserved by default; with preservation off, conversion follows the selected options and prioritizes dedicated FM conjunct glyphs in legacy output.
info.conjunctComparisonNote: Plain consonant combinations and their corresponding glyphs.
info.compactFormsOptionNote: Requires the corresponding option; off by default.
info.touchingSequenceDescription: Touching forms use consonant + ZWJ + virama + consonant; ligated conjuncts use consonant + virama + ZWJ + consonant.

notes.legacyFontsUsuallyDoNotSupportStraightQu: Legacy fonts usually do not support straight quotes; conversion automatically replaces them with curly quotes.
notes.rakarVowelFormsShareLegacyCodes: Legacy encoding cannot distinguish “්‍රු / ◌්‍රූ” from “්‍රැ / ◌්‍රෑ”; both are displayed as “්‍රැ / ◌්‍රෑ”.
notes.legacyFontsLackDedicatedAndGlyphsSoThese: Legacy encoding lacks dedicated glyphs for “ඞ”, “ඞි” and “ඞී”, so they cannot be converted.
notes.theLegacyCodeForWorksOnlyInSomeFontsAnd: Only some fonts support the legacy code for “ඣ්”; others may display it incorrectly.
notes.touchingLettersHaveNoDedicatedLegacyCode: Unicode supports generating touching forms, but legacy encoding has no corresponding slots and displays the letters separately. Original touching layout cannot be preserved and must be regenerated according to the settings.
notes.unicodeDocumentsExportedInEitherModeUseS: Exported Unicode documents do not support custom fonts; they use system fonts by default, falling back to Iskoola Pota when needed.
notes.documentModeExtractsSelectableTextOnlyOr: Document mode extracts selectable text only, discards the original layout, and exports as DOCX.
notes.yourTextIsNotUploadedAutomaticallyPasteA: Your text is not uploaded automatically. Paste a reproducible sample if needed, after removing sensitive information.
